story-and-authority.text: As a validator contributor, I run the Aiken suite and observe precise failures for wrong authorization or token identity behavior, in tests whose names and model references explain the rule.
Everything here is test-only on top of the recorded base; the accepted Lean tree is the authority and no model, validator, or blueprint byte changed.

boundary-repairs-and-controls.text: Three properties had an existential shape: a single unequal result satisfied them, so a partial defect stayed invisible.
Each now asserts the intended outcome exactly for every generated case, with structurally distinct identities.
Old properties passed under deliberate mutations; the new ones fail under the same mutations, and the accepting controls were retained.

authorization-fixture-repair.text: The retract fixtures now use twenty-eight byte owner and signer hashes, matching Cardano key hashes.
Non-owner inequality is structural: generated signers end in a byte the owner cannot have, so the property is purely about authorization.
The accepting and refusing rows share one request and differ only in the signer; and a correct key-hash length is a valid representation, not by itself a complete ledger transaction.
Out-of-window retract rows preserve executable script-failure expectations at the current phase assertion; clean Boolean refusal and its Lean binding move to Issue two hundred five.

refusal-classification.text: Refusal rows distinguish clean semantic outcomes, malformed input failures, and script-level phase-guard failures; the last prove rejection but do not claim a clean Boolean result.
Helper-string reason checks never stand alone; each carries an executable refusal row beside it.

module-organization.text: The three-thousand-line cage test module was split into twelve behavior modules plus a shared fixture module.
Ticket-named modules became behavior-led names, with ticket identifiers kept in the documentation as provenance, and stale currently-broken prose was removed.

name-inventory.text: Every test of the base tree is accounted for: the cage rows move with exactly one rename, and every other rename is a pure ticket-prefix strip. Counts per module are unchanged.

cage-split-inventory.text: This block lists every cage test and its new behavior module: ninety-seven rows, one rename, zero drops.

ticket-prefix-strips.text: This block lists all one hundred sixty-eight prefix renames, old to new, so any reader can verify the mechanical rule rather than trust it.

lean-bindings.text: Citations to absent Lean files are recorded as missing bindings with no conformance claim, and the citations that do resolve are stated with their exact qualified declarations.

verification-and-limits.text: The final staged source passed both existing flake gates: three on-chain checks and two naming-onchain checks; focused runs were controls, not substitutes.
The raw Aiken logs record zero errors but retain non-failing warnings, so the result is not described as warning-clean.

The limits are stated: malformed-context rows bound input shape only, retract phase guards remain script-level until Issue two hundred five, and mutation evidence lives outside the repository because mutations are never committed.
